subject: Merchant ecosystem taxflow — decision log & proposed split billing
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@marketmerchant.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: payments@marketmerchant.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: who is responsible for VAT vs GST on marketplace fees

Hi Priyom / Ben —

Thanks for walking us through the demo yesterday. We have two follow-ups from Tax and Payments:

1) For EU B2B customers where reverse-charge applies, MarketMerchant believes the platform fee should be zero-rated and the merchant should be billed net. Can you confirm Redwood can emit invoices showing platform as a pass-through (no VAT) when provided a valid VAT ID?

2) For APAC GST (Australia + NZ), some merchants are registered and some are not. We need a way to split the platform charge so that our tax engine can calculate GST on the merchant portion only.

We're attaching a quick VAT matrix with our current merchant population by country. Can you propose the minimal invoice metadata and validation steps you need from us to implement both: (a) reverse-charge routing for EU B2B, and (b) split billing for APAC GST?

Best,
Sara Holt
Head of Payments, MarketMerchant

Attachments: vat_matrix_v2.csv

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@marketmerchant.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: who is responsible for VAT vs GST on marketplace fees

Sara —

Thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Quick summary of what Redwood can do today and our proposed minimal integration pattern:

- VAT ID validation: we support an automated VAT ID lookup (VIES for EU) and will mark the invoice line as reverse-charged when validation returns a match and the billing country != merchant country. We need a merchant-record level field: merchant_vat_id and merchant_vat_country.

- Invoice metadata: include three explicit line tags: {platform_fee, merchant_pass_through, merchant_net_charge}. The platform can emit the invoice with the merchant_pass_through lines at zero VAT/RC if merchant_vat_id validated.

- APAC split billing: Redwood can support per-invoice line-level tax code assignment. For Australia/NZ, we recommend the merchant-side charge be a separate line with GST applied by your tax engine. Redwood will accept a 'merchant_tax_responsibility' flag per transaction: "merchant" or "platform". If "merchant", Redwood emits a net amount and a note for your accounts payable to tax the merchant portion.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood sends a short spec (JSON schema) for the invoice payload and the VAT ID validation endpoint we expect.
- Your side adds a nightly batch of merchant VIES checks for pre-validation and a real-time fallback for checkout-time lookups.
- We do a small pilot (200 merchants) where MarketMerchant provides validated VAT IDs and we run 30 days of mirrored invoices to confirm the outputs.

I'll loop in Vanessa for procurement implications and Monica for billing mapping.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quoted message below for context: ""

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@marketmerchant.com>

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: who is responsible for VAT vs GST on marketplace fees

Sara —

Appreciate the detailed ask. Two operational notes from finance:

- When we emit zero-VAT lines for reverse-charge, we must persist the raw VAT-ID validation response (timestamp + VIES lookup id) for audit and SOC2 evidence. Please confirm MarketMerchant can accept a matching audit field in your accounting export.

- For split billing, our preferred approach is to tag the merchant portion with a unique tax code (MM-MERCH-GST-AU, etc.) so downstream systems can reconcile. We'll include the tax code mapping in the payload spec.

Procurement question for Vanessa: do we need a contract amendment to support split-billing line items and different settlement flows?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@marketmerchant.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: who is responsible for VAT vs GST on marketplace fees

Sara —

Quick procurement and rollout notes:

- Contract: we'll push a one-paragraph schedule for tax treatment that states Redwood will follow merchant-supplied VAT IDs and MarketMerchant's election of merchant-tax-responsibility for each transaction. No pricing change; this is a billing-format change. Legal will review the schedule but this should be a lightweight amendment.

- Pilot: approve the 200-merchant pilot (recommended) — duration 30 days. During pilot: Redwood teams will provide daily invoice extracts and a reconciliation template.

- Security & evidence: Monica, please work with Alex Ribeiro at TaxOps (cc'd by Sara) to confirm what fields they need in the audit export.

Sara, if that all sounds reasonable can you: (1) confirm MarketMerchant can provide the merchant_vat_id and a nightly pre-validation batch, and (2) confirm you'd like us to start the pilot the week of 9/13?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
